design_rationale:
WORKLOG / TEST DOSSIER -- task 0 (gap_waiver_cancellations_and_claims, GAP Waiver Premier 150, collision total loss), revision 15 (rework round 14)

1. Draw (scripts/draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems = 3, factor_counts [6, 4, 6, 6]. Assignment (coordinator ruling): gap_ext_premier_deductible_reimbursement 4, gap_ext_claim_starting_balance 6, gap_ext_premier_excluded_amounts 6, gap_ext_claim_worksheet_benefit 6.

2. Why this is a good test. The borrower asks what the GAP waiver pays on her reported collision claim, recorded on the claim. The benefit (root) cannot be worked out on the opening records: the claim carries no balance at loss and no itemized exclusions, and the Premier exclusions wait on the deductible reimbursement that only the borrower claims with her settlement documents. The reimbursement starts from the deductible the insurer actually withheld, up to the plan maximum, and turns on whose declarations are read (the settling insurer's proof, rejected only for a deductible above what the contract allows, not the policy on file), the coverage that paid, how the borrower maximum deductible of the plan the tracking record now carries bounds a withheld deductible above it on a policy put before the company, and the Premier schedule's reimbursement maximum for the loss the claim shows (a collision total loss, the plan's full maximum). The starting balance reconstructs the signed schedule with the odd first period, the due-date change, the SCRA cap, the force-placed premiums capitalized net of the refund credited, and the interest from the latest payment to the loss on the principal in place over that period. The agent reads each prerequisite sentence, sees each waited-on state false, hands the borrower her write and records three more figures.

3. Scope. Task 0 claims the Premier reimbursement, the Premier starting balance, the Premier excluded total and the worksheet benefit with their four tools (claim_premier_deductible_reimbursement_7815b2b6 owner=user, record_claim_balance_at_loss_15fb7d99, record_premier_claim_exclusions_258c7293, record_claim_worksheet_benefit_931d4ebc). Task 1 holds the Plus starting balance and the Plus worksheet benefit (the borrower's acceptance).

4. Problem-tree card (all value_input).
 - BEN -> BAL, state: "The worksheet benefit is not worked out until the claim carries a balance at loss above 0.00." Opening: balance_at_loss_usd = 0.0. Only the Premier starting-balance rule writes a Premier claim's balance at loss. Skipped: benefit 0.00.
 - BEN -> EXC, action: "Before the worksheet benefit is worked out, the claim's excluded amounts are itemized under the Premier exclusion schedule." fallback_reason: the itemization can total 0.00. Opening: excluded_amounts_usd = 0.0. Skipped: benefit 3,730.12.
 - EXC -> DED, action: "The Premier excluded total is fixed only after the borrower's claim for the Premier deductible reimbursement is recorded on the claim." fallback_reason: the reimbursement is 0.00 when a deductible above the plan's borrower maximum was withheld on a policy never put before the company. Opening: primary_deductible_usd = 1000.0, deductible_covered_usd = 0.0. Skipped: excluded total 1,584.05, benefit 2,146.07.
 - Owner=user: the reimbursement claim. Order DED, BAL, EXC, BEN; DED and BAL commute (different fields, no ids, no cross reads).

5. Base-invariant card. Subject gap_claim_opened; gap_claim_benefit's gates apply to gap_claim_filed (met at filing, 14 days after the loss) and gap_claim_decided; base_preconditions policy_scope. Declared overwrites: scheduled balance clause (Premier starting balance, sibling Plus); deductible_reimbursement_basis (Premier reimbursement; the Plus plan restated to the base); excluded_amounts clause, gap_agg_contract_portfolio service-contract refund clause and force-placed premium clause (Premier excluded total, siblings name Plus); excess-LTV clause and ACV/deductible-covered clause (worksheet benefit, sibling names Plus). Every replaced_by restates the base for other plans.

6. Business-object card. Target: the latest claim record of the Premier addendum (reported 2026-08-19, loss 2026-08-05, collision, Keystone Prairie Auto Insurance, ACV 7,700.00, deductible 1,000.00). Decoy: the 2026-03-16 hail claim (withdrawn, no figures), excluded by "latest" and by summing figures on the claim's own loss date. Figures come from the one Tier 2 contract, its tracking record and its DriveSure Powertrain Plus service contract.

7. World (from origination; every contract row priced by the contract product's published documents). Ohio contract signed 2024-02-05 (first payment 2024-03-22, 46-day first period, 72 months, 15,800.00 at 18.49 percent, book value 13,500.00; payments by ACH self-service); tracking record opened on CollateralGuard Plan C (book value), Buckeye Heritage proofs (collision and comprehensive 250.00); due-date change 2024-08-02 (5 installments paid, current, 2024-08-22 -> 2024-09-10, 19 days, within Tier 2's 20); CPI lapse (proof expired 2024-08-05), notices 2024-08-09 / 2024-08-24, placement 2024-09-08 re-banding the record to CollateralGuard Plan B at the 11,800.00 trade-in value (premiums 78.76 and 79.85, both billed 2024-09-08; the latest premium is the one whose billing period starts latest), Buckeye proof 2024-09-20, refund 53.23 credited 2024-09-27, renewal proof 2025-09-10 (the latest accepted proof); extension 2025-05-14 (13 installments paid, seasoning allowance one installment, Tier 2's first extension fee waived); SCRA cap from the duty start 2025-06-02 (request signed 2025-06-05, no interest charged above the cap since the start, installment 213.77) ended 2026-09-01, the day after the 2026-08-31 duty end; Keystone Prairie proof 2026-04-06 rejected for a deductible too high (collision 1,000.00 above Plan B's 500.00), deficient-proof notice 2026-04-08; extension 2026-05-18 (more than 12 months after the first, spacing allowance one installment; Tier 2 fee 25.00, no handling or review charge); June and July 2026 installments unpaid at the loss (oldest 56 days); payment 150.00 on 2026-07-28 applied to interest (150.00 of installment credit); late charges 2026-06-21 / 07-21 / 08-21 / 09-21 at the product's 5.0 percent with the first-delinquency reductions of 50 and 25 percent on the first two (the 08-21 and 09-21 charges fall on installments due after the loss and stay out of the fee part); service contract cancelled for the total loss (processed 2026-08-28) and refunded 162.77 on 2026-09-02, inside its 30-day period; the Buckeye Heritage policy on file expired 2026-09-18 with no acceptable replacement (the Keystone Prairie proof having been rejected), so the tracking record moved to lapse notice with lapse date 2026-09-18 and the first lapse notice was mailed 2026-09-21, inside the 5-day first-notice period (the second notice is not due before 2026-10-06 and placement not before 2026-10-21); frozen 2026-10-05 (117 days past due, below the 120-day charge-off). Decoys: the older accepted proof; the lower comprehensive deductible; the August and September installments due after the loss; the day-prorated service-contract price.

8. Factor cards and sensitivities (handling-time run; each factor's baseline alone, then all at once): gap_ext_premier_deductible_reimbursement: expected 500.0, all-baseline 250.0, per factor pd_policy_at_loss=250.0, pd_paying_coverage=250.0, pd_allowance_test=1000.0, pd_loss_schedule=250.0 | gap_ext_claim_starting_balance: expected 12363.73, all-baseline 11565.51, per factor bl_first_period=12167.24, bl_added_days=12179.51, bl_due_change_count=12183.48, bl_capped_rate_adjustment=12096.2, bl_placed_premiums=12416.96, bl_payment_interest=12346.65 | gap_ext_premier_excluded_amounts: expected 1084.05, all-baseline 2273.74, per factor ep_past_due_count=1297.82, ep_past_due_installment=1235.03, ep_deferral_count=1297.82, ep_deferral_installment=1235.03, ep_placed_premium_basis=1137.28, ep_addon_basis=1189.05 | gap_ext_claim_worksheet_benefit: expected 2646.07, all-baseline 4179.68, per factor bn_term_cut=4019.68, bn_tier_cut=3452.32, bn_band_cut=3855.44, bn_excess_share=2219.9, bn_value_floor=3206.07, bn_floor_value=1456.07.

9. Persona. Danielle Fontaine; volunteers the loss, insurer, report date and goal; gives phone/DOB/ZIP when asked; answers settlement, insurance, salvage, payment, March-claim and service questions consistently with the records (duty 2025-06-02 to 2026-08-31, the customer record's dates); runs the handed tool with the figures given; ends when told the benefit is recorded. No ask beyond the benefit, no hint, no figure steering.

10. Standard solution. Locate, verify, read addendum, claims, contract, ledger, servicing record, signed requests, tracking record and activity, service contract and activity; hand over the reimbursement claim (500.00); record starting balance 12,363.73, Premier excluded total 1,084.05, worksheet benefit 2,646.07.

11. Verification: every value recomputed with check_compute's evaluator on the handling-time world; gates in worklog.md.

12. Draft recomputation from the visible context: reimbursement = lower of the withheld 1,000.00, the rejected Keystone proof's collision deductible 1,000.00 and the plan maximum, never more than the Plan B borrower maximum 500.00 = 500.00; starting balance = signed schedule from the opening principal (amount financed plus 16 first-period days and 15 added days of interest) over 28 installments plus the two-stage cap adjustment, the placed premiums net of the refund and the interest from the 2026-07-28 payment on the principal before the post-loss service-contract refund credit = 12,363.73; Premier excluded total = 63.77 + 38.36 + 213.77 + 105.38 + 162.77 + 500.00 = 1,084.05; benefit = 12,363.73 - 1,373.61 - 1,084.05 - 7,260.00 = 2,646.07. Agrees with gold.
user_scenario:
You are Danielle Fontaine, 32, a dental hygienist in Columbus, Ohio, and a sergeant in the Army Reserve who came off an activation at the end of August. You are calling Harborline Acceptance Corporation, the company that holds your car loan, about the GAP waiver you bought with it. On August 5 your 2019 Chevrolet Malibu was totaled in a collision on I-270. Your insurer, Keystone Prairie Auto Insurance, has settled the car, and you reported the GAP claim to Harborline on August 19, settlement letter in hand. What you want today is simple: you want Harborline to work out what the GAP waiver will pay on that claim and put that benefit on the claim so it can move forward. You are happy for the representative to work the claim figures for you, and you will do your own part if they tell you something needs doing on your end. You speak plainly, a little tired of paperwork, and you do not know how GAP figures are calculated or what your loan balance was on the day of the wreck.

You give your details only when the representative asks for them: your phone number on file is 6145550184, your date of birth is 1994-08-23 and your ZIP code is 43213; if they want something else, your email is danielle.fontaine@outlook.com. If they ask about the insurance settlement, you have the settlement letter in front of you: it shows an actual cash value of $7,700.00 and a deductible of $1,000.00. If they ask about your car insurance, you moved from Buckeye Heritage Mutual to Keystone Prairie on April 1 to save money and sent Harborline the new declarations page; Harborline wrote back that the $1,000 collision deductible was higher than your loan allows, and you meant to lower it but never did. If they ask whether you kept the wreck or whether the insurer took anything off for old damage, you tell them the insurance company took the car to its salvage yard and the letter shows no deduction for prior damage. If they ask about your payments, you admit the June and July payments slipped while you were still on orders, that you sent $150 on July 28, and that you have not paid anything since the wreck. If they ask about the claim you opened back in March, that was hail damage Buckeye ended up repairing, so that claim was withdrawn. If they ask about your service dates, you were activated June 2, 2025 and released August 31, 2026.

If the representative explains that a step has to be done by you yourself and hands you a tool to do it, you use it right away with exactly the figures and reference they give you and read them the confirmation it shows. You do not suggest any steps, amounts or rules of your own, and you do not argue with a figure; if a number sounds odd you simply ask them to double-check it against your records. Once the representative tells you the GAP benefit has been worked out and recorded on your claim, you thank them and end the call.
